wordmark.purpose: kindbeamer, split mid-word by weight: 700 ink against 300 ink-mid. Never split by colour.

display.purpose: Overlay headlines only — AFFIX DOCUMENT (26px/6 tracking), KEYS (15px/6 tracking).

legend.purpose: Section legends (A CONTENTS) and button labels; the section letter goes to wght 700.

label.purpose: TITLE / AUTHOR, dialog group headings, dense button labels.

caption.purpose: Disclaimer line, format tags, franking note, printed key hints.

body.purpose: Everything filled into the form: document names, device names, field values.

status.purpose: The one sentence beside the postmark that names what is happening.

measure.purpose: Sizes, tallies and lane digits, right-aligned in a fixed column that never reflows.

motion.name: postmark-press
motion.purpose: The stamp lands. Fires when the frank state becomes sending, delivered or held. The system's only easing.

motion.name: progress-sweep
motion.purpose: The postmark rim arc and the 2px progress rule above the franking row; not time-based.

motion.name: no-ripple
motion.purpose: Material ink splashes are switched off globally; press feedback is a border strike.

components.name: Press Button (outline)
components.description: The default printed action: a rectangle of ink rule with a tracked uppercase label and, on desktop, its key printed beside it.
components.css: .ds-btn-press { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; height: 34px; padding: 0 16px; background: transparent; color: #16171A; border: 1px solid #16171A; border-radius: 0; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 700; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.4px; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-press .ds-cap { font-size: 9px; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 500; opacity: 0.62; } .ds-btn-press:hover { background: #E9E8E2; border-width: 1.6px; } .ds-btn-press:focus-visible { outline: none; border-width: 1.6px; } .ds-btn-press:disabled { color: #646669; border-color: #C2C1BB; cursor: default; }

components.name: Press Button (solid)
components.description: SEND. The only inverted block on the page; hover knocks a rule out just inside the edge, the way a hand stamp shows its shoulder.
components.css: .ds-btn-solid { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; height: 34px; padding: 0 16px; background: #16171A; color: #F2F1EC; border: 1.2px solid #16171A; border-radius: 0; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 700; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 1.4px; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-solid .ds-cap { font-size: 9px; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 500; opacity: 0.62; } .ds-btn-solid::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 3px; border: 1px solid #F2F1EC; opacity: 0; } .ds-btn-solid:hover::after, .ds-btn-solid:focus-visible::after { opacity: 1; } .ds-btn-solid:focus-visible { outline: none; }

components.name: Tick Box
components.description: The system's only selection control: a 15px square, hairline when off, solid ink with a knocked-out check when on. No switches, no pills.
components.css: .ds-tick { display: inline-block; width: 15px; height: 15px; border: 1.2px solid #7D7F84; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; vertical-align: middle; margin-right: 10px; } .ds-tick-on { border: none; background: #16171A; line-height: 0; }

components.name: Ruled Field
components.description: A form is a ruled line you write on, not a filled box. Press label in a fixed 64px column, Courier value over a hairline that inks and thickens on focus.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; } .ds-field-label { width: 64px; padding-bottom: 7px; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 600; font-size: 9.5px; letter-spacing: 1.3px; color: #52545A; } .ds-field-input { flex: 1; padding: 0 0 4px; background: transparent; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid #C2C1BB; border-radius: 0; font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: -0.2px; color: #16171A; caret-color: #16171A; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: #646669; } .ds-field-input:focus { outline: none; border-bottom: 1.6px solid #16171A; }

components.name: Device Lane
components.description: One fixed-height row per destination: printed key digit, tick box, name. Hovering inks the whole row ground; ticking takes the digit and name to full ink.
components.html: 1Juraj’s Paperwhite
components.css: .ds-lane { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 26px; padding: 0 8px; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: -0.2px; color: #52545A; } .ds-lane-key { width: 12px; margin-right: 9px; text-align: right; font-size: 11px; color: #646669; } .ds-lane:hover { background: #D8D7D1; } .ds-lane-on { color: #16171A; } .ds-lane-on .ds-lane-key { color: #16171A; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Well
components.description: The ruled box where the form expects something to be filled in: one step into the paper, hairline border, square corners. The keyboard's current box takes a 1.2px ink border instead.
components.css: .ds-well { background: #E9E8E2; border: 1px solid #C2C1BB; border-radius: 0; padding: 5px 0; } .ds-well-row { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 26px; padding: 0 10px; font-family: 'Courier Prime', monospace; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.2px; color: #16171A; } .ds-mark { width: 6px; height: 6px; background: #16171A; margin-right: 8px; } .ds-well-size { margin-left: auto; width: 82px; text-align: right; font-weight: 400; font-size: 11px; color: #646669; }

components.name: Postmark
components.description: The only drawn-not-printed element, 48px, five states: idle and ready hairline rings, a sending arc sweeping from twelve o'clock, a solid struck disc for delivered, and thickened rings for held.
components.css: .ds-postmark { width: 48px; height: 48px; transition: transform 190ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-postmark:hover { transform: scale(1.22); }

components.name: Barred Edge
components.description: The airmail border that closes the window top and bottom, and the top and bottom of every dialog slip. It is what makes the window read as addressed post before a word is read.
components.css: .ds-barred { height: 7px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(115deg, #16171A 0 14.3px, transparent 14.3px 26px); } .ds-barred-flip { transform: scaleY(-1); margin-top: 4px; }

components.name: Dialog Slip
components.description: Settings and sign-in: the back of the label. Ground-coloured, max 480px, square, 1.2px ink border, with its own barred edge top and bottom so it reads as the same stock.
components.html:
SETTINGS
APPEARANCE
components.css: .ds-slip { max-width: 480px; background: #F2F1EC; border: 1.2px solid #16171A; border-radius: 0; } .ds-slip-body { padding: 18px 20px 20px; } .ds-slip-head { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 700; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 4px; color: #16171A; margin-bottom: 20px; } .ds-slip-group { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', sans-serif; font-variation-settings: 'wght' 600; font-size: 9.5px; letter-spacing: 1.6px; color: #52545A; padding-bottom: 5px; border-bottom: 1px solid #C2C1BB; }

narrative.overview:
The window is a pre-addressed airmail label printed on e-paper, not an upload dialog. It arrives already filled in — contents, description, addressees from last time — and the only act left is franking it. The barred postal edging closes the window top and bottom, lettered sections A / B / C run down it like fields on a customs declaration, and the send is a postmark pressed into the sheet.

There is one ink and one ground, and nothing else. Every state the app can be in — selected, focused, ticked, sending, delivered, failed — is carried by fill, stroke, tick or inversion. The press face states what the form printed; the typewriter face states what was filled into it. Night is not a dark theme with tinted greys but the same sheet inverted, the way an e-reader inverts: ink becomes ground and nothing is tinted on the way across.

The refused defaults are specific and confirmed: the dark rounded card with a dashed cloud-upload drop zone, toggle switches, accent-coloured pills, and the official client's charcoal-and-orange. The slate-and-teal world this replaced is history, not a reference.
keyCharacteristics: One ink on one ground; no hue anywhere, on either surface.
Night is a true inversion, not a tinted dark palette.
Flat: no shadow, no gradient, no radius — every corner is square (0px).
Two voices: tracked uppercase press type for what was printed, Courier for what was typed.
Rows share one height so counting needs no measuring.
One inverted block per page, and it is SEND.

rules.name: The No-Hue Rule
rules.body: There is no accent colour and none may be added. A state is expressed by fill, stroke weight, tick or inversion — never by a hue. Audit test: a screenshot printed on a mono laser printer must lose nothing.

rules.name: The True Inversion Rule
rules.body: Night maps role for role onto the paper set. Ink becomes ground, ground becomes ink; no channel is tinted, warmed or cooled on the way across, and no component branches on theme beyond picking its Ink0.

rules.name: The Three-Steps-of-Text Rule
rules.body: Text has exactly three weights of presence — ink, ink-mid, ink-faint — and drawn outlines get a fourth, mark. A fifth step is not available; if something needs to recede further, it should not be on the label.

rules.name: The Two-Voices Rule
rules.body: Press type states what the form printed; typed type states what was filled into it. A value the user supplied or a machine measured is never set in the press face, and a legend, button or key cap is never set in Courier.

rules.name: The Printed Key Cap Rule
rules.body: Wherever a key does the same thing as a control, the key is printed on the control in press caption type at 62% ink (ENTER on SEND, ESC on CLEAR, A on ALL, E on the library row, ⌘O / CTRL+O on ADD). On touch builds the caps are dropped entirely — never faked, never drawn as a key-shaped box.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the label floats. If an element needs to separate from its neighbour, it gets a hairline, a well, or a heavier strike of its own border — never a shadow.

rules.name: The One Inverted Block Rule
rules.body: SEND is the only inverted block on the page. Inversion is how the label marks its single irreversible act; a second inverted block would make the act ambiguous. The settings appearance buttons reuse the solid treatment to mark the one active choice, and nothing else may.

dos: Do express every state with fill, stroke weight, tick or inversion. There is no hue in this system and nothing may introduce one.
Do map night role-for-role onto paper via Ink0; read colours through Ink0.of(context) rather than branching on brightness.
Do set printed things (legends, buttons, key caps, tags) in tracked uppercase Libre Franklin, and filled-in things (names, titles, sizes, the state sentence) in Courier Prime.
Do keep every row at one height — 26px on desktop, 48dp on touch — so counting needs no measuring.
Do right-align measurements in the fixed Courier column (82px for sizes) so the column never reflows.
Do make hover and focus a heavier strike of the same rule (1px → 1.6px), or the well as a ground.
Do draw marks — ticks, crosses, the postmark — with painters, in the label's own geometry.
Do drop printed key caps on touch builds and grow targets to 48dp; the same label, simply set larger.
donts: Don't add an accent colour, a tint, a gradient or a coloured status (no red error, no green success). HELD is a heavier ring; DELIVERED is a solid disc.
Don't add shadow, elevation, blur or a translucent scrim. Separation is a hairline, a well, or an inversion.
Don't round a corner. Radius is 0 across the system, including dialogs and scrollbars.
Don't invert a second block. SEND owns inversion on the main surface.
Don't use a toggle switch, a pill, a radio button or a dashed drop zone; selection is the square tick and the drop target is the whole window.
Don't borrow a glyph from a text font as an icon, and don't reach for an icon set: the drawn vocabulary (TickBox, CrossMark, Postmark, BarredEdge) is the whole icon library.
Don't introduce motion beyond the 190ms postmark press and the progress sweep; ripples and splashes are switched off globally.
Don't set a platform UI font. Both faces are bundled so all three platforms print the same label.
